events.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) active at New Orleans after a Questionable tag
events.detail: Jefferson is on the Vikings' active list for the 1:00 ET game at New Orleans after three limited practices with the ankle sprain. His workload is not confirmed. Jordan Addison is inactive (separate item) and Odell Beckham Jr., elevated Saturday, is also inactive, so the receiver depth behind him is thin.
events.so_what: Start Jefferson as a WR1. With Addison and Beckham both out he is the only established receiver, so the target share should hold even if the ankle trims his snaps. Minnesota is on bye in Week 6.

source.label: CBS Sports: NFL Week 5 inactives and injury tracker, Oct. 11, 2026

events.headline: Jordan Addison (hamstring) inactive at New Orleans
events.detail: Addison was downgraded to Doubtful Sunday morning and is on the inactive list. Odell Beckham Jr., elevated from the practice squad Saturday as cover, is inactive too. Justin Jefferson is active.
events.so_what: Bench Addison now; he scores zero. Jefferson absorbs the extra targets and is a locked start. The Vikings bye in Week 6 means Addison is a two-week hole, so plan the Week 6 replacement now.

source.label: CBS Sports: NFL Week 5 inactives and injury tracker, Oct. 11, 2026

events.headline: Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins active at Miami
events.detail: Neither receiver is on the Bengals' official inactive list (S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, TE Jack Endries, WR Colbie Young, DT Landon Robinson). Chase cleared the concussion protocol; Higgins (groin/neck) went from two DNPs to a full Friday. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported both will play.
events.so_what: Start both in their usual WR slots. Chase has no restriction reported. Higgins is the one to watch: an adductor injury two practices ago can mean a lighter snap share, so he is a WR2/FLEX rather than a locked WR1 this week.

source.label: Bengals.com: Six Bengals inactive for Week 5 against Dolphins

events.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle/foot) active at New England despite a Friday DNP
events.detail: Jeanty is not on the Raiders' inactive list (WR Jalen Nailor, QB Aidan O'Connell, S Tristin McCollum, RB Roman Hemby, S Dalton Johnson, G Trey Zuhn III, DT JJ Pegues). He went full, limited, then DNP last week; whether he carries a reduced workload is not reported.
events.so_what: Start him as your RB. The full-limited-DNP trend is the risk: Mike Washington Jr. is the handcuff and steals more work if the foot flares mid-game, so do not chase Washington as a start.

source.label: Raiders.com: Week 5 inactives vs. New England Patriots

events.headline: Terry McLaurin expected active vs. Giants but "likely not a full go"; Stefon Diggs inactive; heavy rain in Washington
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 9 item. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported McLaurin (hamstring) will be active but likely not a full go after he was a game-time decision Sunday morning. Diggs (hamstring) is inactive. Jayden Daniels returns from his elbow injury. Steady rain was falling in Washington before kickoff with water pooling on the sidelines.
events.so_what: McLaurin is a FLEX at best: a limited snap count on a re-tweak-prone hamstring in a rain game is a poor bet, so use a comparable healthy WR if you have one. Diggs is a sit. Rain trims the passing ceiling for Daniels, but his rushing floor keeps him a start.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Week 5 NFL live updates, Oct. 11, 2026

events.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) inactive at Green Bay; Tyson Bagent starts
events.detail: Williams is on the inactive list after a single limited practice Friday, as Ben Johnson signalled when he named Tyson Bagent the starter. Bagent went 25-of-34 for 268 yards and an interception last week against the Jets.
events.so_what: Bench Williams; he scores zero. Bagent is not a fantasy start in a 10-team league. D'Andre Swift's lead-back workload with Kyle Monangai out matters more to Chicago's fantasy output.

source.label: CBS Sports: NFL Week 5 inactives and injury tracker, Oct. 11, 2026

events.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) not expected to play vs. Denver; Quentin Johnston out
events.detail: ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday morning that McConkey is not expected to play after not practicing all week. The Chargers play the 4:25 ET window, so the official inactive list is not out yet. Quentin Johnston (chest) and Brenen Thompson (quad) are already out, leaving Tre' Harris and Oronde Gadsden as Justin Herbert's top targets against a Broncos secondary missing both starting outside corners.
events.so_what: Take McConkey out of your lineup now rather than waiting on a late-window inactive list. Tre' Harris is a FLEX-grade play as the de facto WR1, and Gadsden gains targets too.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Week 5 NFL live updates, Oct. 11, 2026

events.headline: Cardinals finalizing a trade of Marvin Harrison Jr.; he will be inactive Sunday vs. Detroit
events.detail: ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Saturday that Arizona is finalizing a deal for Harrison, and the team told him he will be inactive against the Lions while details are completed. Schefter said no trade will be made until after Sunday's games and named Houston as one team that has held talks; the destination is not confirmed. Arizona's reported asking price was a second-round pick and more. Harrison has 5 catches for 85 yards and a TD this season.
events.so_what: He scores zero this week, so bench him now regardless of where he lands. The new team decides the rest: on an offense with targets to spare his value rises, while a crowded room keeps him a FLEX-level WR. Do not sell him at a Week 5 discount before the destination is known.

source.label: NBC Sports: Schefter, Cardinals finalizing Marvin Harrison Jr. trade

events.headline: D.J. Moore (shoulder) Questionable for Monday at the Rams after a limited Saturday; Joshua Palmer ruled out
events.detail: Moore sat out the first two practices, then was limited Saturday, and Joe Brady listed him Questionable with the decision left until game time. Last week he followed the same pattern, started, and left early after aggravating the shoulder. Palmer hurt his shoulder in Friday practice and is out, so rookie Skyler Bell makes his debut. In Week 4, with Moore out, Keon Coleman played 46 of 59 snaps and went 6-116-1; Khalil Shakir and Coleman are the top two if Moore sits.
events.so_what: A Monday-night Questionable who re-aggravated the same shoulder a week ago is the worst lineup-lock spot of the week: start a Sunday option of similar value over Moore. Coleman is a FLEX-grade play with a downfield TD role whether or not Moore suits up, because Palmer is out too.

source.label: TSN: Bills rule out Oliver, Palmer, wait on WR Moore

events.headline: Steelers place Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on IR; out at least four games
events.detail: Pittsburgh moved Pittman to injured reserve Saturday after he aggravated his left foot (plantar fasciitis, which already cost him Week 2) in Wednesday practice; Mike McCarthy had called it a multiple-week injury. He has 7 catches for 89 yards in three games. Roman Wilson and rookie Germie Bernard are expected to absorb the snaps, and the Steelers elevated WR Brandon Smith for Sunday against the Colts.
events.so_what: IR status means he can sit in an IR slot rather than eat one of the 5 bench spots, so move him there before dropping anyone. Roman Wilson is the speculative add, though a thin Steelers passing game caps his weekly ceiling.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Saturday Oct. 10

events.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) ruled out for Sunday night at Atlanta; Tyler Huntley starts
events.detail: Jesse Minter ruled Jackson out Friday after he missed every practice this week with the left ankle sprain from the Titans game. It is his first missed game of the season. Tyler Huntley starts; he was 2-0 as a fill-in starter last season and went 8 of 9 for 63 yards in relief against Tennessee. Minter would not commit to a Week 6 timeline vs. Cleveland. Zay Flowers (foot) is Questionable after three limited practices; Rotoworld's Friday read is that he is expected to play.
events.so_what: Bench Jackson and pick up or start your QB2 now: this is a Sunday-night game, so there is no late swap if you wait. Huntley is a streaming option only in deeper formats; his legs keep a floor, but 4-pt pass TDs reward volume he will not supply. Flowers is expected to play and stays a start, but Huntley throwing caps his ceiling, and a Sunday-night Questionable means confirming he is active before your early games lock if you have no late pivot.

source.label: ESPN: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson out; Huntley to start SNF vs. Falcons

events.headline: Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith (hamstrings) ruled out for London vs. Jacksonville; Hollywood Brown also out
events.detail: Philadelphia's final report ruled out Barkley, DeVonta Smith (second straight missed game), WR Hollywood Brown (ankle), C Drew Kendall and S Marcus Epps. With Tank Bigsby on IR, Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce are the backs. Dallas Goedert returns from his Week 2 knee injury. Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was limited Friday but carries no designation.
events.so_what: Shipley is a volume FLEX start this week. Three Eagles pass-catchers out concentrates targets on whoever is left, so the returning Goedert goes straight back into the TE slot in a format this shallow at the position. Wicks is the only healthy depth receiver and a one-week dart, not a FAAB target.

source.label: ESPN: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith among 5 Eagles ruled out vs. Jaguars

events.headline: D'Andre Swift (hip, knee) cleared, no designation for Sunday at Green Bay
events.detail: Swift went DNP Wednesday and limited Thursday, then came off the Bears' injury report entirely Friday. With Kyle Monangai ruled out, he is the lead back. He was benched in the third quarter last week after his second fumble of the season.
events.so_what: Start Swift as an RB2/FLEX on lead-back volume. The fumble benching is the one risk to the workload; Roschon Johnson is the only other back.

source.label: PFT: Bears rule Kyle Monangai out for Week 5

events.headline: Kyle Monangai (toe) ruled out at Green Bay, in a boot and week-to-week
events.detail: Ben Johnson ruled Monangai out Friday; the toe, not the thumb, is the real problem. He is in a boot and now week-to-week. Caleb Williams is Questionable after a limited Friday.
events.so_what: Bench Monangai. His week-to-week tag makes a short IR stash reasonable if you have the slot open, rather than burning one of 5 bench spots. D'Andre Swift takes the lead-back work.

source.label: PFT: Bears rule Kyle Monangai out for Week 5

events.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) Questionable vs. Vikings; Chris Olave and Tyler Shough carry no designation
events.detail: Kamara missed Wednesday, then practiced Thursday and Friday (limited on the official report) and is Questionable. Olave was upgraded to full Friday and has no game designation despite the foot issue added Thursday. Shough (left hand) practiced fully Thursday and Friday and is also off the report.
events.so_what: Kamara is a probable start; the back injury argues for a managed snap count, so treat him as an RB2/FLEX rather than a locked RB1. Olave is a normal start.

source.label: WWL/Audacy: Saints rule out three players; Kamara questionable

events.headline: CeeDee Lamb's quad injury called a bruise, not considered serious; expected back for next game at Green Bay
events.detail: Lamb had 2 catches for 9 yards before leaving Thursday's 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay in the fourth quarter, returning for one snap and exiting again. On Friday NFL Network's Ian Rapoport described it as more of a quad bruise than a strain, "not considered to be major," and said Lamb should return after the long weekend for the Cowboys' next game, Sunday night at Green Bay on Oct. 18. Brian Schottenheimer called it "pretty painful." George Pickens caught 9 of 13 targets for 130 yards and a TD in the loss. This is a report, not a clearance: the first Cowboys practice report next week is the fact to set a lineup on.
events.so_what: Lamb's points for this week are already banked, and the extra days off work in his favour. Plan on him as a WR start for the Green Bay game, pending the first practice report. Pickens stays a locked WR start either way. Flournoy is now only a contingency add, since the reporting points to Lamb missing no game time.

source.label: Newsweek: Cowboys get encouraging CeeDee Lamb injury update after TNF loss

events.headline: Bucky Irving runs for 165 yards and a TD as Tampa Bay piles up 241 rushing yards behind rookie Jalon Daniels
events.detail: In the 24-16 Thursday win at Dallas, Irving had a career-best 21 carries for 165 yards and a rushing TD plus a receiving score. Kenneth Gainwell had 7 touches. Daniels, in his second start for the injured Baker Mayfield, went 19 of 25 for 189 yards and a TD with no turnovers and 23 rushing yards. Emeka Egbuka caught 6 of 9 targets for 38 yards and scored on a 14-yard run.
events.so_what: With a rookie QB, Tampa Bay leaned on the run, and Irving's 21-to-7 split over Gainwell is a lead-back role worth an RB2 start every week Mayfield sits. Daniels protected the ball but is not a fantasy start. Egbuka's 9 targets keep him a FLEX on volume even on a short-passing day.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Buccaneers-Cowboys Week 5 TNF live updates

events.headline: Mike Evans (ribs) cleared, no designation for Sunday at Seattle
events.detail: Evans sat Thursday and was limited Friday, then came off the 49ers' final injury report with no game designation for Sunday at Seattle (reported by ESPN's Adam Schefter). An early version of one 49ers report had him Questionable; the final report does not. He already played through the rib injury in Week 4 and led the team in receiving.
events.so_what: Set him as a WR starter. He played through this same injury two weeks ago, so the risk is an in-game re-aggravation rather than a reduced role.

source.label: NBC Sports/PFT: 49ers WR Mike Evans has no injury designation, Oct. 9, 2026

events.headline: Malik Nabers (knee soreness) cleared, no designation for Sunday at Washington
events.detail: Nabers missed Wednesday with a sore knee and was limited Thursday, and John Harbaugh said Friday, "He'll be ready to play Sunday." The Giants' final report carries no designation for him; Cam Skattebo (shoulder) and Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) are also clear. He is back from last season's ACL and meniscus tears.
events.so_what: Start him in a WR slot. The knee history still makes his snap share worth checking after the game rather than assuming a full workload.

events.headline: Breece Hall (quad) and Adonai Mitchell (finger) ruled out vs. Browns; Braelon Allen leads again
events.detail: The Jets ruled out Hall for a second straight game, and Adonai Mitchell (finger, hurt in practice Sept. 24, no procedure) misses his third straight; Aaron Glenn says Mitchell is progressing faster than expected. Braelon Allen has been the lead back with Hall sidelined. Mason Taylor (thumb) returns after a full practice week. Glenn still calls Hall week-to-week.
events.so_what: Hall stays out of lineups until he strings practices together. Allen is a volume FLEX with the backfield to himself. Mitchell's absence concentrates targets on Garrett Wilson.

events.headline: Jayden Daniels (elbow) cleared, no designation vs. Giants; Mariota (MCL) avoids IR
events.detail: Daniels practiced fully all week and carries no designation for Sunday against the Giants after missing last game; he will wear a brace on his left arm. Marcus Mariota sprained his right MCL in London and was not placed on IR. Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is out and Terry McLaurin is Questionable (separate item).
events.so_what: Start him. His rushing is the konami premium that makes him a QB1 in this scoring; with Diggs out and McLaurin uncertain the passing ceiling is capped this week, so the floor rests on his legs.

events.headline: Brock Bowers, Dallas Goedert, Mason Taylor, Jeremiyah Love and Cam Skattebo cleared, no designations for Sunday
events.detail: Friday's final reports carry no designation for Bowers (knee), Goedert (knee, missed last game), Mason Taylor (thumb, missed last game), Love (ankle, called a maintenance issue) or Skattebo (shoulder). Also clear: Chris Olave (foot), Tony Pollard (foot), Jakobi Meyers (thumb) and Mark Andrews (hand). Keenan Allen (groin) is Questionable but practiced fully Friday.
events.so_what: Each is a confirmed start in his usual slot. Goedert and Taylor return to shallow TE pools, so a streamer from last week can go back to the bench. Allen's full Friday puts him on the play side of Questionable.

source.label: RotoWire: Week 5 Friday injury report, Oct. 9, 2026

events.headline: Sean Payton takes play-calling back from Davis Webb starting Week 5 vs. the Chargers
events.detail: Payton confirmed Thursday that he will call the offensive plays Sunday, reversing February's handoff to OC Davis Webb. Webb keeps a significant game-planning and game-day role and may stay in Bo Nix's headset, per ESPN. Denver is 2-2 with a bottom-six offense in both yards and points. Seattle visits Denver the following Thursday.
events.so_what: A play-caller change is a usage shift the projections have not priced. Give Bo Nix and the Broncos' skill players a game before moving them up or down; two games in five days gives a fast read.

source.label: NBC Sports: Shocker: Sean Payton reclaims play-calling duties

events.headline: Tank Dell returns to Texans practice, opening his 21-day activation window
events.detail: Dell practiced Wednesday for the first time this regular season after opening the year on IR, recovering from the multi-ligament knee injury he suffered in December 2024. Houston now has 21 days to activate him or leave him on IR. No game date has been set.
events.so_what: Not a lineup option yet; he is a stash. A bench stash costs one of only five bench spots, so it is worth it only on a roster that can carry a no-points slot for two or three weeks.

source.label: Yahoo Sports NFL live updates, Oct. 7, 2026

events.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) could miss several weeks; Tyquan Thornton out 12 to 16 weeks after ankle dislocation
events.detail: Rice pulled up on a first-quarter catch-and-run against the Raiders and did not return. Andy Reid called it a tweak, but The Athletic's Mike Silver reported Rice could be out several weeks. Kansas City has its bye in Week 5, so the first game he can miss is Week 6 against the Chargers. Thornton dislocated his ankle in the fourth quarter and needs surgery, with a possible late-season return.
events.so_what: Hold Rice through the bye and read the Week 6 practice reports; this is a bench stash, not a drop. With Thornton gone for months, the Chiefs' remaining receivers and tight ends absorb Mahomes' targets, so watch which one runs the most routes in Week 6.
